name: silence
lore:
# On the Transmutation of Quiet: Silence

To cast *Silence* is to seize the local resonance of the Weave and pull it taut until it snaps into a vacuum. As you shape the magic, the air grows heavy, pressing against your eardrums like the weight of deep water. Visually, the affected sphere manifests as a subtle, oily shimmer—a distortion where light loses its vibrancy, as if the world itself has held its breath.

Legend attributes its discovery to Master Aristhone of the Silent Library. Besieged by the cacophony of a warring goblin horde, Aristhone did not reach for fire. Instead, he reached for the stillness of the void. He draped a "shroud of nothingness" over his sanctum; it is said the invaders grew so unnerved by the absolute absence of their own war-cries that they fled, believing they had stumbled into the realm of the dead.

For the wise adventurer, this spell is the ultimate gag for the loquacious spellcaster. Remember: sound is the bridge between thought and manifestation. Break the bridge, and the wizard is but a man waving his hands in the dark.
